doc.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020

title: Marine Corps training and the Corps Four at El Toro
summary: Boot camp in San Diego, the Marine band at El Toro, then the Corps Four quartet on a TV show and later a radio show.

venues.name: El Toro Marine Corps Air Station

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. So I understand you ended up playing in a group called the Dress Blues?
The Corps Four. That was the name of the group.

And well I went into the Marine Corps, you know I went through the boot camp and the infantry training and all of that stuff. So when I was assigned I remember the recruiter, once I’d decided that I would join, he says, “Yeah, man, well you can go to Parris Island,” I said whoa, stop right there. I said, “I am not going to Parris Island.”

I had heard about Parris Island. And he said, “Well what about, you could go to MCRD,” the Marine Corps Recruit Depot, which is in San Diego. I said well that sounds a little better. So I’ll do that. You know. So that’s what I did. And I went through the training, basic training, there, and then in [inaudible] — I’m thinking California, I’ll think of the name of it. It’s nothing but hills. And it was after boot camp that we went and all we did was run up and down them hills man, you know. So when my orders came after I finished with the training, they give you a ten day leave, and my orders came to report to El Toro, at the time, El Toro was an air base where fighter pilots trained and there was a band there attached to that particular branch — not branch —

See the main station at El Toro was like stable, stationary. Like the people who were there, they were there to sort of run the base. The air wing was a part of what they called Air Pacific which meant that the training was preparing Marines, if anything happened in the Pacific these were the guys who were going to go first. But the base, if you were on the base with, I don’t know what it would be called, then you would stay there. But the band was a part of Air Pacific so if they went then the band went with them. If it happened you know. So I was in the Marines band at El Toro and a guy came up to me one day, he was a sergeant. He said, “Hey man, how’d you like to be on T.V?” You know and I’m looking at him and I’m saying, “Hey, man, that’s a funny joke, right?” He said, “No, man,” He said a piano player, his enlistment was up. So we need a piano player in the group. So I said yeah, okay, I’ll go and audition for that. So I did and I was accepted into that group. It was four players. That’s why it was called the Corps Four: guitar, string bass, drums, and piano. And that’s what I did. The T.V. show lasted maybe about a year after I got on there, or a year and a half, something like that. So then the lieutenant who was in charge, he got this radio show which featured us, basically doing the same thing we were doing on the T.V. show but it was on his radio show. And I did that until my enlistment was up.
So that was pretty much what I did.
